259	A 3D view sketches on its work plane (`workplane.rs`), as Revit's Work Plane > Set and more: `View3D::work_plane`, a `WorkPlane` on a
260	`level` (a GUID, in `visit_refs!`), through three `points`, or on a `surface` picked on the model (a point and a normal), each moved
261	`offset` mm along its normal; with none, the lowest level (`Model::work_plane`). `WorkPlane::resolve` gives it as a `workplane::Frame`,
262	a point and a unit normal, at any angle, upright too: three points along a line are refused (`workplane::through`, facing up unless
263	upright), and `Model::check` resolves it. `Frame::over_plan` is it as a `walls::Plane` over the plan, as a floor's top is, for a sketch
264	that stays plan lines raised onto it (none for an upright one); `Frame::axes` are its level and up directions. The `work_plane` command
265	sets it (making the default 3D view, as `section_box` does), moves the plane as it is given only `offset`, or, given nothing, clears it;
266	deleting its level clears it too. `workplane::host` is the level what is made on it stands on: the highest at or below the plane, else
267	the lowest; a floor, a ceiling, a roof or a shaft is made only on a level one (`workplane::is_level`, the desktop's check). The scene
268	says what a work plane is picked from: `Scene::face_at`, the face under a pixel (where, which way toward the camera, and the element's
269	triangles in its plane), and `Scene::corner_near`, the corner within so many pixels that nothing nearer hides, both of what the view's
270	look shows and inside its section box.
271	`Camera::on_slope` finds the point of such a plane under a pixel, `Camera::at_depth` a pixel's point at a depth, and the 3D pictures
272	say what point of the model a pixel shows (`Image::point`, from the depth the processor's picture now keeps; `gpu::Mesh::point`).
273	
274	A 3D view may be cut to a section box (fork issue 1), as Revit's Section Box: `View3D::section_box`, a `SectionBox` of six planes
275	square to the axes from `min` to `max`, `on` or off (off, it keeps its extents), set by the `section_box` command (which makes the
276	default 3D view, as `graphics` does, and with no extents fits the box round `Model::model_box`, `SECTION_BOX_ROOM` clear of it), and
277	checked in `Model::check` (usable numbers, `MIN_SECTION_BOX` between the planes on each axis). `Look::of` carries a view's box while
278	it's on (`Look::section_box`; `with_section_box` puts another in, for a box being dragged), and `Scene::picture` cuts to it: the view
279	is square on, so `Boxed` turns a pixel and its depth into a model point with one sum, and `raster` keeps a pixel only where that point
280	is in the box (a triangle wholly past one plane is passed over first), `dots` a scan's point only where it is, and the wireframe each
281	edge as far as it runs inside (`within`, Liang and Barsky's clipping). What it cuts away isn't drawn, so it isn't picked; the edge
282	where a cut face meets paper is drawn as any edge is, and cut faces aren't capped yet. A level whose plane is above or below the box is
283	left out, and the rest are cut to its sides. A section's picture has its own clip and ignores the box. The card doesn't cut yet:
284	`Mesh::new` refuses a boxed view, and the processor draws it. Its grips are the core's: `box_grips` (the middle of each face: west,
285	east, south, north, bottom, top), `box_edges`, `move_box_face` (a face moved along its axis to 10 mm, stopping short of the face across
286	from it) and `Camera::along` (how far, mm, a drag on the picture moves a point along an axis; none for an axis pointing at the camera).
287	A plan may follow the box (`section_box` on a `Level` or a `PlanView`, set by `modify`; a dependent view follows its parent's,
288	`Model::plan_box`; Duplicate View copies it): while the default 3D view's box is on, the plan shows what the box keeps, its range
289	from the box's bottom up to its top, where it cuts (`Model::shown_range`), and its crop the box's sides, within its own crop if it has
290	one (`Model::shown_crop`). What a plan draws and snaps to reads those; `plan_range` and `crop_of` stay the plan's own, which commands
291	(dimensions, joins, Duplicate View) and Properties use. A ceiling plan keeps its own range.
292	Visibility/Graphics lists each tab's categories alphabetically by their translated display names. Projection and cut pattern
293	cells edit independent foreground and background overrides, using the project's fill patterns (including imported PAT patterns),
294	colours and a combined preview. Unchecked layers inherit; `<None>` explicitly hides a layer. OK/Apply submits the draft as one
295	`graphics` command; Clear Overrides clears only that cell. Annotation categories expose projection patterns for filled regions.
296	Styles hold `foreground` and `background` as optional `{pattern: name | null, color: [r,g,b]}` layers, alongside the existing
297	`fill` colour. Element, filter and category precedence resolves each layer separately. Plans, reflected ceiling plans, section
298	cuts and regions draw the layers with the same bounded pattern renderer as filled region types; the pattern's drafting/model
299	target sets its scale. Pattern references follow library renames, save as GUIDs, and prevent deletion while used by a view or
300	template. The 3D renderer continues to use the solid `fill` colour for shading; it does not draw hatch patterns.

302	A 3D view may be seen in perspective, as through a camera, rather than parallel (axonometric): `View3D::perspective`, a `Perspective`
303	with the `lens` it is seen through (its focal length, mm on a 35 mm camera, whose 36 mm of film, `FILM`, is the picture's width; 10 to
304	600 mm, checked in `Model::check`) and `on` or off (off, it keeps its lens), set by the `perspective` command, which makes the default 3D
305	view as `section_box` does; `View3D::lens` is the lens while it's on. The camera is `view3d::Camera` with `lens` set: the eye stands back from
306	the target along the view as far as makes `scale` true at the target (`Camera::eye_distance`, the focal length in px over the scale), so
307	orbit turns it about the target, pan carries both, zoom walks it in (a point on the plane through the target staying under the cursor),
308	`Camera::sized` keeps the eye where it stood as the picture or the lens changes, and `with_eye_elevation` raises or lowers it looking at the
309	same target from as far across the plan. `fit_from` fits a perspective with the eye as far back as puts a ball round what is shown inside
310	the picture's narrower side. `Camera::project` keeps "larger is nearer": in perspective `d² / a - d` for a point `a` mm in front of an eye
311	`d` from the target, as near as a parallel view's at the target and straight across the picture of a plane (it goes as `1 / a`), so the
312	rasterizer's barycentric depths stay exact, and `point_at` turns a pixel and its depth back into the model point (textures, the section
313	box's `Boxed`). What is less than `NEAR` (10 mm) in front of the eye is cut away: a triangle into the one or two its near part makes
314	(`Projector::in_front`, as weights of its corners, so a curve's lighting carries over), a line to its near part (`Camera::in_front`: edges in
315	wireframe, levels' marks, the section box's frame); a point behind the eye projects to no number. A face is lit on the side the eye is on
316	(`Camera::toward`), as the card's `front_facing` is, and how far a line may lie behind a surface and show is a pixel's worth where the
317	line is (`Camera::slack`). `Camera::along` takes, in perspective, the point on the axis nearest the line from the eye through the pointer,
318	so a dragged section box face stays under it. `render` of the 3D view goes through its lens, and `eye_elevation` puts the eye that high. A
319	sheet's 3D viewport stays parallel (its scale is paper's). The card draws perspective too: `View::perspective` gives the shader the
320	focal length, how far the eye is and a depth of `a + b / ahead`, 1 at `NEAR` and 0 past the far side of the mesh (a reversed depth, as
321	precise far off as near), with the same `NEAR` cut by the card's clipping; `Mesh::pick` cuts and projects as the processor does.
322	`picking_the_mesh_in_perspective_finds_what_the_cpu_picture_shows_from_afar_and_from_within` and
323	`the_card_draws_in_perspective_what_the_processor_does_from_afar_and_from_among_the_walls` compare them, from outside and with the eye
324	inside the house (`view3d::inside`).

326	A 3D view may have a **camera of its own**, as Revit's Camera tool makes one: `View3D::camera`, a `ViewCamera` holding the model
327	point its `eye` stands at and the `target` it looks at (both `[x, y, z]` mm), with the view's `perspective` on. The `camera` command
328	makes a new named view from an eye and a target (the eye never on the target, checked in `Model::check`), gives one to an existing
329	view (the default `{3D}` among them, made by name as `perspective` makes it), or, with a `view` and none of `eye`, `target` or
330	`lens`, reads one back (`null` eye and target for a view with no camera yet — reading makes nothing). A view that already has a
331	camera keeps the point a change leaves out, so `lens` alone or one point alone changes just that; a view without one needs both.
332	`view3d::Camera::at` builds the render camera from the
333	eye, target and lens, its azimuth and elevation the direction from the eye to the target and `scale` the focal length over the
334	distance, so `Camera::eye` is exactly the eye given; `view3d::camera_of` does the same for a view and a scale, for a sheet's 3D
335	viewport. On the desktop the Camera tool (View tab) clicks an eye then a target in a plan, each at a height over it from the Options
336	Bar, and opens the new view: `BimApp::active_3d` is the 3D view the 3D tab shows (a camera view by id, or none for the default),
337	`BimApp::open_3d` sets it (and resets the on-screen camera, so the view stands from its own camera), the Project Browser lists every
338	3D view under 3D Views. Properties (`camera.rs`, `BimApp::camera_properties`) is one panel bound to a view: the 3D tab passes the
339	view it shows, and a camera view picked on a plan passes the picked one, so both show the same Name, Eye, Target and Focal Length
340	and edit it the same way (`camera` for the camera, `modify` for the name). Graphics, phasing and the section box stay with the view
341	on screen (`graphic_view`), not with a camera view picked on a plan: its mark shows its camera, its project parameters and its
342	phase. A camera view shows no Azimuth or Elevation: those
343	(`View3D::azimuth`, `View3D::elevation`) only frame a 3D view **without** a camera on a sheet (`sheet::framing`, `camera_of`), so a
344	view on a sheet whose view has a camera shows its name alone. A camera edit while its view is on screen drops the on-screen
345	camera (`Orbit::camera`), so the next frame stands the view from the model and the settled hand has nothing old to write back. A
346	camera view's mark is drawn on its level's plan
347	(`render::camera_mark`, the level from `Model::camera_level`): a symbol at its eye, a dashed line to what it looks at, pickable so a right
348	click opens the view (`Action::OpenView`) or a double click does. Orbiting, panning or zooming a camera view writes its eye and target back
349	once the hand and the wheel have let it be (`view3d` reads the on-screen `Camera::eye` back into the view), so leaving it and returning comes
350	back to where it was left. A camera moved elsewhere — its mark dragged on a plan, a command, undo — moves the view already showing
351	it: `Orbit::built` holds the camera the picture was built from, and a difference with the model's means the picture stands from the
352	model anew instead of its old camera being written back over the move; a floating window, drawn while the hand works in another
353	view, writes nothing.

356	The 3D view can be drawn on the graphics card (File > Settings > Performance; off until asked for: `BimApp::card`, `settings.json`'s
357	`gpu_3d`). `view3d::gpu::Mesh` is the triangles a view shows as f32 vertices relative to the middle of what is drawn (millimetres far
358	from the origin would overflow f32), each with its colour, normal, face normal, plane, element and texture; the textures' mip levels as
359	words (`Skin`; `Mesh::lookups` gives the level a zoom looks up, as `Sampler::level_for` does); and a bounding volume hierarchy built on
360	the first pick. Surfaces seen through come after the opaque ones (`Mesh::clear_from`), each element's transparency in its `Owner` (an element whose layers differ in transparency has an `Owner` for each).
361	`Mesh::new` refuses, with a reason, what the card doesn't draw (hidden line, wireframe, more than `MAX_TRIS`), and the processor draws those as before, and sections and sheets always. `Mesh::pick` is `Image::pick` without a picture: the
362	same projection and barycentric test for triangles (the nearest seen through where it is nearer than the nearest opaque one), and for levels the same `LevelMarks` that `Scene::picture` draws (`level_marks`: one
363	definition of a level's lines and head). The desktop's `gpu.rs` and `gpu.wgsl` draw it in passes into a texture egui shows like the
364	processor's picture: the opaque surfaces (lit as `picture` lights them, textured as `Sampler::at` looks up), those seen through (the
365	nearest in front of the opaque depth, in targets of their own), then an edge wherever the opaque plane changes between a pixel and the one
366	to its right or below, else the surface tinted halfway where selected, with what is seen through blended over it, and the levels' lines
367	where nothing opaque nearer hides them. What changes between pictures is the camera and the lines; the owners' tints and the textures'
368	lookups are written again only when they change. A change to how
369	the processor shades, draws an edge or marks a level goes in the shader too: `the_card_draws_what_the_processor_does` and the core's
370	`picking_the_mesh_finds_what_the_cpu_picture_shows` compare them (and, seen through,
371	`the_card_draws_what_the_view_sees_through_as_the_processor_does` and `picking_through_what_the_view_sees_through_finds_what_the_cpu_picture_shows`), and skip on a machine with no graphics adapter. The card is for Vulkan, Metal and DirectX 12: on 
372	OpenGL wgpu panics in the shader compiler for what the shaders read (a depth texture; buffers in a vertex shader), so `Gpu::new` refuses it, and puts whatever else a compiler stops at under `catch_unwind`.
373	The card is made the first time it is wanted (`Card::ready`: compiling its shaders is not a start's cost), and one that can't be made says why on the Performance page.
374	A device error is caught
375	in the card's own error scopes, never left to wgpu's handler (which ends the program), and hands the view to the processor for good.

377	A 3D view's **Graphic Display Options** (Revit's GD) are `View3D::display`, a `view3d::DisplayOptions`: `edges` (on unless turned
378	off; only Shaded leaves them out, as Hidden Line and Wireframe always draw them), `silhouette` (an outline that many px wide, 0 to
379	`MAX_SILHOUETTE`, 10, checked in `Model::check`; 0 for none) and `ambient_shadows` (off unless turned on), set by the
380	`graphic_display_options` command (GD; it makes the default 3D view as `section_box` does, keeps what is left out, and with
381	nothing given reads them back). `Look::of` carries them (`Look::display`), so the desktop, a sheet's 3D viewport and `render`
382	draw them alike; a section's picture ignores them. Both come off the opaque depth the rasterizer already has, before a scan's
383	dots are in it, in nearness as `Camera::project` gives it, measured in pixels' worth (`Camera::slack`), so they read the
384	same parallel and in perspective. Ambient shadows (`view3d::ambient`) are a screen-space pass: for each pixel, the pixels
385	across from each other at eight offsets (`AMBIENT`, 4 to 12 px, four lines at two reaches); over a plane the depth runs
386	straight, so their mean is the pixel's own, and only where the surfaces round it rise toward the eye on both sides (a corner,
387	the foot of a wall on a floor) does it darken, by `AMBIENT_DARK` of its light at most; a neighbour more than `AMBIENT_REACH`
388	pixels' worth a pixel off in depth is something else, in front or behind, and counts for nothing, so nothing casts a halo. A
389	silhouette (`view3d::outlines`) is wherever two neighbouring pixels are one on a surface and one on nothing, or on different
390	planes `OUTLINE_GAP` (4) pixels' worth apart in depth: each pixel whose square `width + 1` across (from `width / 2` before it)
391	holds such a pair is drawn in the edge's colour, so a straight outline is exactly `width` px wide. The card does the same in
392	`fs_post` (`ambient`, `outlined`, `worth` in `gpu.wgsl`, the options in the globals' ninth vector, from `Mesh::display`), so
393	no pass is added: `the_card_draws_edges_silhouettes_and_ambient_shadows_as_the_processor_does` compares them. Cast shadows
394	from a sun are not drawn yet. The desktop's dialog (`display.rs`) opens by GD and from the view control bar's Visual Style
395	menu, alike in both looks of the window, and runs the command on the 3D view on screen.

397	The 3D scene can be exported as glTF 2.0 binary, for Blender and other viewers (`gltf.rs`: `save` to a `.glb`, which the CLI's `--save` and
398	`convert` and the MCP server reach too, and File > Export > 3D Scene as glTF in both profiles). It writes the triangles of `Scene::facets`,
399	the ones the processor's picture and the card's mesh are made of, as the default 3D view shows them (`Look::of_3d`): its phase and phase

400	filter, its design options, what Visibility/Graphics hides, and the colours and transparency it paints, linked models included
401	(`extras.linked`). A section box on that view is not applied, the whole of each element shown is written, and neither are textures, edges,
402	levels, point clouds or the camera. There is a node and a mesh for each element, the node named by the element's id with its `id`, `guid`
403	and `category` in `extras`, and a primitive in the mesh for each colour the element is shaded in (a compound wall has one for each layer).
404	A primitive's material is the scene's sRGB colour in linear light, as glTF's base colour is, blended with alpha `1 - clearness` where the view
405	sees through the surface (a mass is, by default), and always double sided, as the scene draws both sides of every surface. Positions are in
406	metres, turned and not mirrored: east stays x, up becomes y and north becomes -z, so the winding is kept. Curved surfaces keep their smooth
407	normals, vertices that agree in position and normal are shared within a primitive, and a triangle with no area is left out. A scene past
408	`gltf::MAX_TRIS` (the card's limit) is refused with how many triangles there are, and an empty one with what to show. The tests read the
409	chunks back (header, lengths, alignment, the JSON, a box's bounds and volume); the Khronos validator (`npm i gltf-validator`, then
410	`validateBytes`) reports no errors, warnings or hints on the sample house and on the 20-storey tower of `run --highrise`.

412	The 3D view works round what is under the cursor, on both painters. What a pick finds has a point: `view3d::Surface` is the
413	element, the model point where the line of sight through the pixel meets the surface the picture shows there, and its normal turned
414	toward the camera. The processor's picture finds it from the triangle its pixel holds (`Scene::surface_in`), the card's mesh from
415	the triangle its pick finds (`Mesh::surface`), and on a level's mark it is the level's plane; `orbit.rs`'s `Picker::surface` asks
416	whichever drew the picture on screen. A drag orbits round the surface's point under the pointer where it began
417	(`Camera::orbit_about` turns the whole camera about it, so the point keeps its pixel, in perspective too), round the target where
418	nothing is; the wheel zooms toward it (`Camera::zoom_about` closes the target and the eye in on it), and with nothing under the
419	cursor zooms about the cursor as before. `the_surface_under_a_pixel_is_the_same_through_the_mesh_as_the_picture_and_an_orbit_or_a_zoom_about_it_keeps_it_there`
420	checks the two painters agree, and `tests/working3d.rs` drives it in both profiles, on the card where the machine has one.

422	The 3D view's tools draw on a **work plane**, as Revit's (`workplane.rs`): `work_plane` takes the surface under the cursor and,
423	for a face that is level and turned up (a floor's top, a flat roof's, a level's plane), gives the level its points go on (the face's
424	element's own level, a level's plane that level, else the highest level at or below it) and the offset over it, to the micron;
425	with nothing under the cursor, the lowest level's plane, the ground. A face that isn't level, or is turned down, gives none, and
426	the status line says what the tool draws on. Every drawing tool takes its points so in the 3D view (`orbit.rs`'s `aim`), and each
427	point snaps as its level's plan snaps (`snap3d`: `snap::snap` on the plane's level, from the points the tool has picked, Shift squaring
428	the step, within the snap's points as the plane is foreshortened there; else the nearest 10 mm). The Wall tool (WA): the first
429	point's plane holds for the rest of the chain, whatever the cursor passes over, and each wall goes through `place` as in a plan, with
430	`base_offset` from `Orbit::wall_base`, which `wall_params` reads while the 3D view places a point. A run's tool (beams, wall footings,
431	pipes, ducts, conduits, cable trays, wires, conductors, cabling) takes each end on the face it is clicked on, so a run from a floor's
432	top to a wall's or a column's top climbs (`place_run_lifted`: `offset` and `end_offset` over the start's level, the Options Bar's
433	offset over each): that is a brace; where nothing is under the cursor, its end stays on its start's plane. Column (CL), Structural
434	Column and Isolated Footing stand on the face (`place_column`, `place_stand_lifted`: `base_offset`, or a footing's top `offset`, its
435	height over the level), and Component (CM) and the MEP fixtures run `component` with that level and offset. `Orbit::plane` keeps the
436	last point clicked and its plane, which a chain or a run's end takes only while it is the tool's own point before. The point under the
437	cursor is drawn as a plan's snap, naming what it snapped to (a free point: Nearest, of the element whose face it is), with the wall
438	or run from the point before and its length. Where neither a level face nor the ground meets the line of sight, the tool says what
439	it needs (`needs_face`, by the tool's title). Floor and Ceiling sketch on the view's work plane (below), which may be set on a level
440	face picked on the model.

442	A level's own plan is the level (its `view_range`, `crop` and `graphics` are the level's); every other plan of it is an `Element::PlanView`
443	(Revit's Duplicate View: `duplicate_view`, which only plans take). A plan has a key: the level's id, or a plan view's. `Model::plan_level` says
444	which level a key shows, and everything that draws or measures the model takes that level (`draw_plan`, `plan_shows`, the canvas's tools), while
445	what is the view's own takes the key: its graphics (`graphics_of`), view range (`view_range_of`, which a template may control), crop (`crop_of`)
446	and annotation. Annotation says which view it is in: a note or a spot elevation by `view`, a dimension or a tag by an optional `view` beside its
447	`level` or its host (none: the level's own plan), and `Model::annotation_in` asks whether a plan draws it. A command that takes a `level` takes a
448	plan view too (`plan_param`): what is built stands on its level, what is dimensioned or tagged is in the view. A dependent view (`parent`) follows
449	its parent's view range and graphics (`plan_source`; `graphics`, `scale`, `detail` and `visual_style` refuse it, naming the parent), has a crop
450	of its own and draws its parent's annotation as well as its own. Deleting a view deletes what is annotated in it and its dependents; a level
451	takes its plan views with it. A project that has none writes the same file as before. A plan's own name, lettered at its bottom left, is in the drawings that make an image (`plan`, `ceiling_plan`: `titled`), not in the window's (`draw`, 
452	`draw_ceiling`) or a sheet's (`draw_at`), where the tab and the viewport's title say it. The desktop: View > Duplicate View, DP, and the Project
453	Browser's right-click, which also has Delete for a plan view; `Sheet::Plan` and `Sheet::Ceiling` hold the key.

455	Fill patterns, filled region types and filled regions (`fills.rs`) follow line patterns and styles. A `FillPattern` is
456	families of parallel lines as a PAT file has them (`HatchLine`: an angle, an origin, a spacing across, a shift along, and
457	dashes, a space negative and a dot 0), drafting (mm on paper, so the same at any scale) or model (mm in the building); no
458	lines, it fills solid. `fills::strokes` lays a pattern over any outlines with holes (inside an odd number of rings), each line
459	cut to the view's window (what lies past it is never counted or drawn), and gives up rather than draw past a cap: more than
460	50,000 strokes, or more work than `fills::MAX_WORK` (a line tried against every edge, a dash stepped over), which bounds a
461	dense pattern over an outline of thousands of corners and dots a twentieth of a millimetre apart. A pattern that gives up draws
462	none of its lines and says so in `Drawing::notes` (`the fill pattern of element 100012 has more lines than a view can hold at
463	this scale`), which the `render` command returns as `notes` for plans and sheets; a front end can show them. `FillPattern::check`
464	wants a dash (a dot, 0, is one), a space and a pattern at least `MIN_SPACING` long in a family's dashes, so a list of spaces
465	only draws nothing and never trips a cap. `render::filled_region` draws a region's
466	masking (paper), its background and its foreground pattern, then its boundary's sketch lines, each in its own line style
467	(`SketchLine::style`, a library reference as the region's is) else the region's, or not at all (`invisible`, or a region
468	of invisible lines with none of its own); in sketch mode the Options Bar's Line Style is what the lines drawn take, and the
469	lines picked take it at once. A plan draws its regions after the model and before the annotation, in a loop of their own (sections
470	and sheets likewise), so a masking region hides the walls under it but not the note on it. A `FilledRegion` is annotation of
471	its view (`Model::annotation_plan`, so a duplicated plan has its own) and its sketch is a `sketch::SketchLine` list, solved
472	when drawn, any number of outlines; Edit Boundary edits it as any other. Patterns and region types are library entries,
473	renamed with their references (a type follows its patterns, a region its type and line style) and refused deleted while
474	used. The desktop has Annotate > Region (Filled Region, FR, and Masking Region, sketch mode with the type and the line style
475	in the Options Bar), Properties (the Type Selector above the instance fields, Line Style with invisible lines), and Manage >
476	Annotation Settings > Fill Patterns (`fillpatterns.rs`: the patterns as one draft, each a name, drafting or model and a
477	swatch; one of whole lines (Simple Lines, `FillPattern::whole_lines`) edited line by line with Edit Lines (an angle, an origin
478	and a spacing each: a shift only staggers dashes, and dashed patterns are drawn and made with Custom), one made of lines
479	redefined from lines (Redefine, as wide as Edit Lines), any other (dashed, imported or a starter's) kept as it came, and Import and Export of PAT files at the right, Replace imported by same name saying what an import does
480	with a name the list has; region types are edited from a region with Edit Type, on the same draft).
481	
482	A custom pattern is made of lines drawn, as pyRevit's Make Pattern makes one (`fills::make`, the `make_fill_pattern` command):
483	the detail lines picked, all of one view, cut to the rectangle between two corners (the tile), each a family that runs on into the
484	next tiles' copies of itself. A line repeats only at a slope `(i W, j H)` of whole tiles (`i`, `j` at most `MAX_STEPS`, 48), so one
485	drawn at another is turned to the simplest such slope within `TURN` (0.25°), else the nearest; its family's dashes are its length
486	and a space to the repeat `L = |(i W, j H)|`, its lines `W H / L` apart, each shifted along by the lattice's other vector
487	`(c W, d H)`, `i d - j c = 1` (Euclid's). A line on the tile's edge and its copy on the opposite one are one family; curves go as
488	their drawn points' chords. A model pattern is as drawn; a drafting one is the drawing on paper at the view's scale, which the
489	pattern keeps (`FillPattern::drawn`, saved with it): turned from one to the other (the dialog's Type, or `fill_pattern`'s `target`
490	without `lines`), it is rescaled (`retargeted`), and the dialog offers Redefine for it where a simple one has Edit Lines, which
491	picks the lines and corners again and keeps its name and type. A pattern holds at most `MAX_FAMILIES`
492	(256) families. In the desktop, New Pattern > Custom hides the dialog while the lines are picked as anything is (Enter, or the
493	right-click menu's Finish), then the corners (`Tool::PatternCorner`), and brings it back with the pattern previewed: OK, Pick
494	Again, Cancel. Esc, another tool or another view brings the dialog back. `pat.rs` reads and writes PAT files (`;%UNITS`,
495	`;%TYPE`, a negative offset stepping the other way; a pattern that can't be one left out with why) for the dialog and for the
496	`import_fill_patterns` and `export_fill_patterns` commands. A PAT file is hostile input: `read` stops after `MAX_PATTERNS`
497	(2,000) patterns and counts the rest, `Read::left_out` names the first `MAX_LEFT_OUT` (100) with `left_out_count` for all, a line
498	is cut at 22 fields and a bad one is echoed to 40 letters, a family whose dashes are all spaces is left out, and a file over
499	`MAX_TEXT` (16 MiB) is refused unread. A byte that isn't UTF-8 is read as the Latin-1 letter with its number, which is right
500	for accents and not for Windows-1252's punctuation at 0x80 to 0x9F. The description after a pattern's name isn't kept. The
501	`import_fill_patterns` command takes the file's `text` up to that size too (a name is limited to 256 letters, a file isn't) and
502	replies with the first 100 `left_out` and `left_out_count`.
503	
504	Edit Type opens a region's Type Properties from either a selected region or an active sketch: select a type, create a
505	new one, duplicate one with its settings, or rename it. Foreground and background each have their own pattern (including
506	None) and color; masking controls whether paper hides geometry underneath. The combined preview shows both layers and
507	a sample line behind them, so masking can be checked before applying. The Patterns tab edits and creates patterns in
508	the same draft. Apply and OK update definitions and the selected instances in one transaction; a type edit affects every
509	region of that type, a duplicate is assigned only to the selected instances or the active sketch, and Cancel discards
510	unapplied work. Duplicate or blank names are refused without replacing another definition. Renames preserve library
511	identity and update the active sketch's type reference. The palette's Type Selector and Edit Type use the same region
512	types as the Options Bar.
513	
514	The instance parameter grid has no second Region Type field: the Type Selector is the type control. Non-masking regions
515	replace model backgrounds while retaining visible cut outlines, cut foreground patterns (including solid foregrounds),
516	and projected model lines. `render/regions.rs` finds the drawing's ink once (the model layer's lines and patterns, less what a
517	later fill covers, so a low wall hidden by a cut wall does not reappear; and a section's or elevation's hidden-line picture as
518	runs of its pixels, which is all the ink an elevation has) and gives each region the part of it in its area: the outline less
519	its holes, inside an odd number of rings, less the masking regions drawn before it. A line is kept where it lies in the area or
520	within half its stroke of it (its pen's width as it will draw, from the owner's object style while the pen is not set yet), so a
521	region edge sketched on a wall face keeps the whole face; Visibility/Graphics weights wider than the object style's are not
522	allowed for. Lines are cut by the rings and the masks as they are, never by boolean operations on polygons (which are cubic in
523	the corners an outline can have): only the model's filled patterns are, by the pieces of the area they reach. The pieces of a
524	polyline that meet stay one line, so its corners keep their joins, and a dashed line's dashes stay where they were (the dashes of
525	the cycle a piece begins in are solid lines of their own). A section's ink belongs to the region that keeps it (`Part::Pattern`),
526	so a sheet's viewport, which keeps what an element owns, has it. A caller that has the section's picture (the desktop's, a sheet's,
527	`section_png`'s) hands it in (`render::section_over`, `section_at_over`), at the view's size or a multiple of it (a screen with more
528	pixels to the point), and the ink is the picture's own pixels, as runs: a row of a pixel's height, and a run of up to two pixels
529	that sits on one of the row above (the edge of a tall wall) joined to it as one vertical line, so 200 walls 20 m tall at 4000 x 2600
530	px are some hundreds of lines and not a million runs. A picture of more than 250,000 runs (noise, not drawings) keeps the first
531	250,000 and the drawing's `notes` say the ink of the last rows is under the region. `render::section` draws a picture of its own
532	when a non-masking region wants one, which costs what the picture does, every call. Masking still hides the model; detail annotation remains above the
533	region. The same display list feeds the desktop, PNG, SVG and sheet viewports.
534	
535	Limits, kept as Revit has them or not yet built: a non-masking region with a solid background hides a room's tag text while its outlines
536	stay (Revit keeps room tags above filled regions: not verified); grids, levels and room fills are drawn before the regions, so a masking
537	region hides them; there is no Bring to Front or Send to Back, a region is over the model and under the annotation, in the order of its
538	id; Move and Rotate carry a region's or a floor's model pattern with it (`pattern_origin`), where Revit may leave a model pattern fixed in
539	the building, and Align moves it; a filled region drawn on a sheet itself is plain annotation over the viewports, so a solid one hides
540	what lies under it (Revit has no regions on sheets).
541	
542	Sketch snapping (`snap::in_sketch`) combines the visible model's wall faces and slab edges, detail lines and existing
543	region boundaries in the active view, and the draft's own lines. It supports endpoints, midpoints (of each segment of a
544	polyline), intersections (where two walls meet is one too), perpendiculars, nearest points and angle guides, the anchors of
545	annotation (a note's insertion point and leader, a tag's head, a dimension's stations, a spot elevation, section and elevation
546	marks, detail groups and repeating details), and a camera's eye and target rather than its mark's body or name, honoring Manage > Snaps
547	and one-point overrides. An element being edited is omitted as a model snap target; its draft supplies the boundary instead.
548	Rectangle and arc previews use the same origin points and Shift constraint as a click. Annotation in another independent view,
549	or hidden by Visibility/Graphics, is excluded. A plan view cuts where its own view range says (`plan_range` of the view, not of its
550	level); a section or an elevation has no plan to snap to, only its own detail lines and regions. Of what the plan builds, the
551	nearest `MAX_OUTLINES` elements within reach have their outlines snapped to (one `walls::Index` for them all), and the nearest
552	`MAX_NEAR` chords are tried against each other. Ceilings snap in a floor plan as well as a ceiling plan, because a snap does not know
553	which of the two the cursor is in, and the members of a detail group are not snap targets.

556	[region editing](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2026/ENU/Revit-DocumentPresent/files/GUID-183D9B1E-6554-4C19-9EA9-B32C8D2A5C9D.htm),
557	and [sketch snaps](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2022/ENU/Revit-Customize/files/GUID-A3947840-1F30-41D7-AF75-B61687952A07.htm).
558	Boundary weights follow each boundary line's style. See also Autodesk's [region masking 
559	behavior](https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Filled-Region-with-solid-fill-does-not-cover-all-elements-in-Revit.html).

561	A material's cut and surface may be one of the project's fill patterns (`Material::cut_pattern`, `surface_pattern`, a
562	library reference like a region type's), over the patterns drawn in code (`model::Pattern`), which stay for the materials
563	that name them: `material` takes either name for `cut` and `surface`, and the desktop's material editor lists both. A fill
564	pattern a material shows can't be deleted, and is renamed with it. `render::fill_pattern` draws a fill pattern for a
565	region, a cut layer (its courses along the layer) and a floor's or a ceiling's surface. A model pattern is aligned and
566	rotated as Revit's: a filled region and a floor hold `pattern_origin` and `pattern_angle` (`fills::strokes_placed`), which
567	Move, Rotate and Mirror carry with the element; Align with a pattern line picked second (`render::pattern_line_at`) moves the
568	origin so that line lies on the reference, and Properties shows Pattern Angle. `Model::align_pattern(id, reference, line)` is
569	that arithmetic (the origin moved across by the gap between the two parallel lines, to the micron; the error says when the
570	element has no model pattern, or the lines aren't parallel or have no length), so every front end gets the same answer and
571	sets it with `modify`. `pattern_origin` and `pattern_angle` are in the `modify`, `filled_region` and `floor` command docs, and
572	`elements` shows them for a region and a floor even at their defaults.

574	## Linked models
575	
576	A `Link` element (`link.rs`; commands `link` and `reload`) is another project shown in this one as a reference. The file holds its name, its
577	path, where its origin stands (`at`) and a turn (`angle`); what it read is `Model::loaded`, by path, outside the file (`serde(skip)`), filled by
578	`link`, `reload` and `open` (`relink`, which doesn't follow the links of a linked file). The views draw `link::seen(model)`: the project with
579	each loaded link's built elements (`built`: not its views, sheets, annotation, detail lines, filled regions, detail groups, rooms, grids or links) moved and turned by `commands::transformed`
580	and brought in with `insert::insert_as(.., linked: true)` under ids from `LINKED` up (`ids.rs`), so `link::is_linked(id)` tells them; a level of the
581	link at the height of one of the project's (1 mm) is that level, another comes in named `link: level`. Everything that takes a `&Model` draws and snaps to
582	them without knowing: `Look::with` makes a linked id halftone, and picking never answers one (`Drawing::pick_all`, `in_box`, `Image::pick`,
583	`in_box`, `shows` and `Mesh::pick` leave them out). The commands that make an image (`render`, `save` to svg, png or pdf) draw `seen`; the desktop's
584	`view_model` does, cached by the project's `Arc`. The schedules, `Model::check`, IFC and every command that edits work on the project itself.
585	To do: shared coordinates, a link's graphics overrides and visibility per view, hosting on a linked wall, unloading.

587	## Dimensions
588	
589	A dimension (`Dimension`, the `dimension` command) measures the model as it is, so it follows what it measures. Its `refs` are lines
590	(`Reference {id, face}`: a wall's centre line, faces and ends, a door's or window's centre and jambs, a grid, a straight detail line) or, with
591	`point: start|end`, the point at that end of one (`Model::reference_point`: a wall's centre line ends where its location line does, a face where
592	the outline turns off it, so at the mitred corner; a detail line of any shape at its ends; `reference_points` lists them, `endpoint_at` finds the
593	nearest, `{endpoint: [x, y]}` in a command). `reference_geometry` gives either as a line, a point as a line of no length, and `crossings` lays
594	them along the way the dimension measures (`measured_along`): a linear one's `orient` (horizontal or vertical), else square to its first line,
595	else from its first point to the next elsewhere. `Model::check` refuses a line not parallel to the first, or not square to a linear one's line,
596	and points all in one place. Mirror keeps the end of a line along the element and flips the one across it (`Reference::mirrored`); Flip swaps
597	both. A linear one given no `orient` runs vertical where `at` is east or west of everything it measures, else horizontal; the desktop's Auto
598	(`dims::Placing::kind`) also lays an aligned one where the cursor is among the points (`Orient::follow`), as Archicad does. Radial and diameter
599	dimensions measure round columns, curved walls (centre line or a face) and circles and arcs (`reference_arc`); arc length, a curved wall's or an
600	arc's length along it (`reference_sweep`), all of it or, with two point references after the arc, between them (`Model::arc_span`), its line an arc through `at` round the same centre. `dims::round_at` picks the face nearest a click.
601	
602	Each dimension has a dimension type (`dims.rs`, `Model::dimension_types`, a library entry `Kind::DimensionType`, the `dimension_type` command),
603	Revit's type parameters with lengths in mm on paper: Dimension String Type (continuous, baseline, ordinate), tick mark (diagonal, arrow, open
604	arrow, dot, none) and its size, line and tick pens, colour, dimension line extension, Witness Line Control (gap to element, or fixed to the
605	dimension line with its length), witness line gap and extension, baseline spacing, centre marks, and its text: font (as text types take one,
606	`DimensionType::lettering`), size, bold, italic, underline, width factor, offset, opaque or transparent background, Read Convention, units and
607	rounding (`DimensionType::length`), and the radius and diameter symbols and the equality text. A project starts with `Diagonal - 2.5mm Arial`,
608	which aligned, linear, angular and arc length dimensions start in, and `Arrow - 2.5mm Arial`, which radial and diameter ones do
609	(`dims::default_type`); a file of format 9 gives its dimensions their kind's (`Model::typed_dimensions`). A dimension's own text, Revit's
610	instance values, is a prefix, a suffix, text above and below, Replace With Text and Equality Display, and a segment may have its own over it
611	(`texts`, `SegmentText`, the `dimension_text` command; `Dimension::text` reads one through the other, `dimension_segment_at` finds a segment by a
612	point); `Model::dimension_labels` is what its
613	numbers read (and `elements` shows as `labels`): a baseline string's each from its first reference, an ordinate's each witness line's, the first 0.
614	An aligned or linear dimension may be kept equal (`equal`, Revit's EQ, which also turns its Equality Display on) and have segments
615	locked at a length (`locked`, `Lock`; the `dimension_constraint` command). `constraints::keep` runs in `Session::execute` after every undoable
616	command, before the check: each constrained dimension is solved on its own line (its `stations`, each with its reference), a locked segment tying
617	two stations rigidly and equality tying all its segments to one length (a locked one's, else its ends', which stay where they are, so an inner
618	reference dragged goes back); a run of tied stations stays where what the command moved puts it, else where its first is. What has to move is
619	moved by `commands::move_by`, as `move` moves it, and the dimensions are solved again (`PASSES`) until all hold; where they can't (locked
620	lengths that differ made equal, one element pulled two ways), the command is refused, saying which dimension, and nothing changes.
621	A length typed for a segment (`dimension_value`; in the window, a click on the selected dimension's number, as a temporary
622	dimension's takes one) moves what the segment ends at, its second station's reference, along the dimension by the difference
623	(`move_by`), and a locked segment is locked at it; the other locks then hold or the command is refused. Align with `lock` (Revit's
624	padlock: in the window, the open padlock Align offers on the line it moved) leaves a lock: a dimension of the aligned line's reference
625	and the reference's (`to`, else whatever has a line along it), its one segment locked at 0 and `alignment` set, which
626	`constraints::keep` holds as it holds the others, so the two lines stay on one line whatever either is moved by; one that can't hold
627	with the other locks is refused, and the project is as it was. A lock is drawn by a front end, never on paper (`render/dimensions.rs`
628	draws nothing of it): the window shows each locked segment's shut padlock whether its dimension is selected or not, and each alignment
629	lock's padlock beside where its lines meet, which a click unlocks (deletes). Format 15 holds them; 14 would read one as a dimension of
630	nothing.
631	`render/dimensions.rs` draws them all as the type says (`Ink`: its lines, ticks and witness lines, and its numbers laid out by `crate::text`
632	over the paper where the background is opaque).
633	
634	A 3D view has dimensions of its own (`Element::Dimension3D`, the `dimension_3d` command; `dims3d.rs`), as Revit's aligned dimension in a 3D
635	view: two references (`Ref3`), each a point of the model or a point on an edge (its two ends with it), and a point its line passes through,
636	kept by the view (`view`, a GUID: deleting the view takes them with it) and of a dimension type as a plan's are. Between two points it measures
637	straight from one to the other; to an edge, square to the edge's line, so between two parallel edges it is how far apart they are
638	(`dims3d::ends`). They hold places in space, not references to elements: moving an element leaves them, and `move`, `rotate` and `mirror`
639	take them in plan when they are moved themselves. They draw as marks (`dims3d::marks`, `Mark`: a polyline in the picture's pixels, its width
640	and colour), through any camera and at any paper size (`SCREEN` pixels a paper millimetre on screen, `sheet::DENSITY` on a sheet): a
641	witness line from each end of what it measures to its line, its line, a tick at each end and its number lettered along it in our strokes
642	(`font.rs`), reading from the left, on the side away from what it measures; nothing hides them. `dims3d::paint` paints marks into the
643	processor's picture, which the `render` command does for a 3D view; a sheet draws them as its own lines over the view's picture, so they print
644	in its PDF; the window draws them over the picture on either painter (the card's too) with the theme's ink, the selection's colour when
645	picked. Visibility/Graphics hides them with Dimensions (`category_of`). In the window the Aligned Dimension tool (DI) in the 3D view picks a
646	corner seen within the snap's reach (`Scene::corner_near`), else an edge within a pick's (`Scene::edge_near`, the point of it nearest the
647	cursor), else the point of the face there; after two, a click places the line where it meets the plane through the two that faces the
648	camera most (`dims3d::line_through`), and the status line says how long it is. In Modify a click on a dimension's lines picks it before what
649	the picture shows under them (`dims3d::pick`).

200	all of one view, into a group type (`Model::detail_groups`) holding them as `Member`s about the middle of them, in no
201	view, and puts one `DetailGroup` element in their place. Members are parts (`HasPart`, `parts_now`): each has its own id
202	and GUID, and their line styles and region types are library references like an element's (`lib_refs_mut`), so renames
203	reach them; `Model::check` holds each to what the same element in a view must be (`annotation_ok`). A placed group is an
204	origin, an angle and `mirrored`; `groups::placed` gives its members as elements of its view (through
205	`commands::transform`, as Move and Rotate take elements), which `render::detail_group` draws, regions under lines and notes,
206	all owned by the group, so it picks, moves, rotates and mirrors as one. `ungroup` (UG) puts those elements back in the view;
207	`group_type` renames a type (its groups follow) or deletes it while nothing is of it. A `RepeatingDetail` places a group
208	along a line every `spacing` from its start, each turned along it (at most `MAX_REPEATS`), as Revit's Repeating Detail
209	Component does with a detail component. A view draws every member of every group and repeat in it each time, so
210	`Model::check` caps what one view places: a group counts its type's members, a repeating detail its members once for each
211	repeat, and `MAX_PLACED` (10,000) is the most in a view (measured with the probe `probe_the_cost_of_the_most_hatched_regions_a_view_may_place`,
212	10,000 hatched regions take about 0.1 s to draw at 3 m across and 0.5 s at 30 m across, 2.8 million primitives, on a machine that
213	is not busy, in a dev build (the core is built at opt-level 2 there) and in release alike, and up to 0.29 s and 1.10 s in the dev
214	build on a busy one; the 200,000 it once allowed took 6 s and 30 million primitives). A placed member that is a huge circle costs
215	more (the probe `probe_the_cost_of_placed_members_that_are_huge_circles`: 8,192 points each, about 0.2 ms to draw and 3 to 5 ms to
216	rasterize, 8 ms on a busy machine), so a view at the cap of them can take a minute or more to render; the cap stays. A member note keeps its own angle under a pure mirror
217	(it still reads the right way round) and turns with the group's angle. The file holds a group's members as elements, and
218	`Model::read` leaves out of them what this build doesn't know, as it does for any element
219	(`/detail_groups/<name>/members/<i>/element/...`). Deleting a line style that a filled region or a group's member is drawn in
220	is refused with the region's or the group's name. On the desktop, Annotate > Detail has Detail Group, Repeating Detail and
221	Create Group, and the right-click menu has Create Group and Ungroup.
222	
223	A project with any of this (line styles and patterns, fill patterns, region types, detail lines, regions, groups, repeating
224	details, sketches) needs file format 6, and every file is saved as 6 now, with or without any of it: a build that reads up to 5
225	would fail on one with a serde error, so 6 makes it say that the file is from a newer BIMCraft (even for a plain project). Nothing
226	in a file of 5 changes, so `Model::migrate` has no step for 5 to 6.

228	The Options Bar's Offset puts a line, an arc or a polyline beside the points clicked; a rectangle, a polygon or a circle grows
229	by it as a whole (`grown`, its corners joined), and a spline or an ellipse takes none (`Shape::offsets`). Modify's Offset takes
230	ellipses and splines too, as a spline through points within `FIT_TOL` of the true offset (`curves::offset_fit`), refused where
231	it would fold over itself. While a shape is drawn its numbers can be typed (`draw::numbers`, `reading`, `typed`): a rectangle's
232	width and height (Tab between them, the canvas taking the Tab from egui's focus), a circle's or a polygon's radius, the third
233	point's radius, angle or reach; anything else typed is a length toward the cursor, as a line's, in sketch mode too. The canvas
234	labels them as they read (`shape_dimensions`). A spline or a polyline finishes with Enter, a double click or the right-click
235	menu's Finish Drawing; Fillet Arc previews the arc nearest the cursor and its radius, Offset a dashed ghost of the copy, and
236	Trim/Extend and Fillet's picks so far show in the selection's colour. Trim/Extend to Corner with two lines or walls selected (or
237	two sketch lines picked) joins them at once, each keeping the part toward its middle.
238	
239	`Drawing::detail` is the level the plan or the section is drawn at: coarse leaves out a compound element's layers and an opening's
240	symbols, medium its patterns (`cut_layer`, a floor's `surface`), fine draws as before. In the 3D view `Look::style` picks how
241	`Scene::picture` draws: shaded as ever, hidden line as a section's picture is (paper faces, edges), wireframe by `Scene::edges` (where
242	surfaces meet at an angle or end, found once) drawn through the faces; a pixel within two of a line picks its element.
243	
244	A view's graphics (`graphics.rs`; `Level`, `Section` and `View3D` each hold `graphics`) hide and override by category, by view
245	filter (`Model::view_filters`: categories and a schedule filter's rules, `schedule::picks`) and by element: an element's own beats
246	the filters' (the first applied prevailing), which beat the category's, and hiding by any of them hides. `Look::of` resolves a
247	view to what it hides and how it paints the rest; the drawing code asks `look.shows(id)` wherever it loops over elements (plans,
248	sections, `cut_outlines`, `seen_below`, `view3d::Scene::picture`) and `look.dress` recolours the finished `Drawing` by owner and
249	by `Part` (`Drawing::part` marks what is drawn as projection, cut, lettering or hatching (and the lines between layers), so a
250	new drawing of what a view cuts sets `Part::Cut`; a hidden door's opening is drawn owned by none, the wall's; the cut walls' union fill has no owner and takes its colour at the draw site, `cut_unions`). A view template
251	(`Model::view_templates`), for a kind of view (`ViewKind`: plans, elevations and sections, or 3D views; `from` sets it, none is any),
252	controls groups of the views that follow it (categories, filters, a plan's view range through
253	`Model::view_range_of`, a phase with its phase filter, design options, scale, detail level, visual style), and they can't change those
254	(`graphics`, `scale`, `detail`, `visual_style` and `modify` refuse). Snaps, Tag All, the desktop's Select All
255	Instances and the framing of sections and 3D views take what `Look` shows too. A level's ceiling plan is its plan's view;
256	transparency shows in 3D only. A surface is seen through as much as the greater of its material's `transparency` (`Tri::alpha`, in
257	plain views too) and the view's override for its element (not in a plain view); both painters take it from `Tri::alpha`.
258	
259	A 3D view sketches on its work plane (`workplane.rs`), as Revit's Work Plane > Set and more: `View3D::work_plane`, a `WorkPlane` on a
260	`level` (a GUID, in `visit_refs!`), through three `points`, or on a `surface` picked on the model (a point and a normal), each moved
261	`offset` mm along its normal; with none, the lowest level (`Model::work_plane`). `WorkPlane::resolve` gives it as a `workplane::Frame`,
262	a point and a unit normal, at any angle, upright too: three points along a line are refused (`workplane::through`, facing up unless
263	upright), and `Model::check` resolves it. `Frame::over_plan` is it as a `walls::Plane` over the plan, as a floor's top is, for a sketch
264	that stays plan lines raised onto it (none for an upright one); `Frame::axes` are its level and up directions. The `work_plane` command
265	sets it (making the default 3D view, as `section_box` does), moves the plane as it is given only `offset`, or, given nothing, clears it;
266	deleting its level clears it too. `workplane::host` is the level what is made on it stands on: the highest at or below the plane, else
267	the lowest; a floor, a ceiling, a roof or a shaft is made only on a level one (`workplane::is_level`, the desktop's check). The scene
268	says what a work plane is picked from: `Scene::face_at`, the face under a pixel (where, which way toward the camera, and the element's
269	triangles in its plane), and `Scene::corner_near`, the corner within so many pixels that nothing nearer hides, both of what the view's
270	look shows and inside its section box.
271	`Camera::on_slope` finds the point of such a plane under a pixel, `Camera::at_depth` a pixel's point at a depth, and the 3D pictures
272	say what point of the model a pixel shows (`Image::point`, from the depth the processor's picture now keeps; `gpu::Mesh::point`).
273	
274	A 3D view may be cut to a section box (fork issue 1), as Revit's Section Box: `View3D::section_box`, a `SectionBox` of six planes
275	square to the axes from `min` to `max`, `on` or off (off, it keeps its extents), set by the `section_box` command (which makes the
276	default 3D view, as `graphics` does, and with no extents fits the box round `Model::model_box`, `SECTION_BOX_ROOM` clear of it), and
277	checked in `Model::check` (usable numbers, `MIN_SECTION_BOX` between the planes on each axis). `Look::of` carries a view's box while
278	it's on (`Look::section_box`; `with_section_box` puts another in, for a box being dragged), and `Scene::picture` cuts to it: the view
279	is square on, so `Boxed` turns a pixel and its depth into a model point with one sum, and `raster` keeps a pixel only where that point
280	is in the box (a triangle wholly past one plane is passed over first), `dots` a scan's point only where it is, and the wireframe each
281	edge as far as it runs inside (`within`, Liang and Barsky's clipping). What it cuts away isn't drawn, so it isn't picked; the edge
282	where a cut face meets paper is drawn as any edge is, and cut faces aren't capped yet. A level whose plane is above or below the box is
283	left out, and the rest are cut to its sides. A section's picture has its own clip and ignores the box. The card doesn't cut yet:
284	`Mesh::new` refuses a boxed view, and the processor draws it. Its grips are the core's: `box_grips` (the middle of each face: west,
285	east, south, north, bottom, top), `box_edges`, `move_box_face` (a face moved along its axis to 10 mm, stopping short of the face across
286	from it) and `Camera::along` (how far, mm, a drag on the picture moves a point along an axis; none for an axis pointing at the camera).
287	A plan may follow the box (`section_box` on a `Level` or a `PlanView`, set by `modify`; a dependent view follows its parent's,
288	`Model::plan_box`; Duplicate View copies it): while the default 3D view's box is on, the plan shows what the box keeps, its range
289	from the box's bottom up to its top, where it cuts (`Model::shown_range`), and its crop the box's sides, within its own crop if it has
290	one (`Model::shown_crop`). What a plan draws and snaps to reads those; `plan_range` and `crop_of` stay the plan's own, which commands
291	(dimensions, joins, Duplicate View) and Properties use. A ceiling plan keeps its own range.
292	Visibility/Graphics lists each tab's categories alphabetically by their translated display names. Projection and cut pattern
293	cells edit independent foreground and background overrides, using the project's fill patterns (including imported PAT patterns),
294	colours and a combined preview. Unchecked layers inherit; `<None>` explicitly hides a layer. OK/Apply submits the draft as one
295	`graphics` command; Clear Overrides clears only that cell. Annotation categories expose projection patterns for filled regions.
296	Styles hold `foreground` and `background` as optional `{pattern: name | null, color: [r,g,b]}` layers, alongside the existing
297	`fill` colour. Element, filter and category precedence resolves each layer separately. Plans, reflected ceiling plans, section
298	cuts and regions draw the layers with the same bounded pattern renderer as filled region types; the pattern's drafting/model
299	target sets its scale. Pattern references follow library renames, save as GUIDs, and prevent deletion while used by a view or
300	template. The 3D renderer continues to use the solid `fill` colour for shading; it does not draw hatch patterns.
301	
302	A 3D view may be seen in perspective, as through a camera, rather than parallel (axonometric): `View3D::perspective`, a `Perspective`
303	with the `lens` it is seen through (its focal length, mm on a 35 mm camera, whose 36 mm of film, `FILM`, is the picture's width; 10 to
304	600 mm, checked in `Model::check`) and `on` or off (off, it keeps its lens), set by the `perspective` command, which makes the default 3D
305	view as `section_box` does; `View3D::lens` is the lens while it's on. The camera is `view3d::Camera` with `lens` set: the eye stands back from
306	the target along the view as far as makes `scale` true at the target (`Camera::eye_distance`, the focal length in px over the scale), so
307	orbit turns it about the target, pan carries both, zoom walks it in (a point on the plane through the target staying under the cursor),
308	`Camera::sized` keeps the eye where it stood as the picture or the lens changes, and `with_eye_elevation` raises or lowers it looking at the
309	same target from as far across the plan. `fit_from` fits a perspective with the eye as far back as puts a ball round what is shown inside
310	the picture's narrower side. `Camera::project` keeps "larger is nearer": in perspective `d² / a - d` for a point `a` mm in front of an eye
311	`d` from the target, as near as a parallel view's at the target and straight across the picture of a plane (it goes as `1 / a`), so the
312	rasterizer's barycentric depths stay exact, and `point_at` turns a pixel and its depth back into the model point (textures, the section
313	box's `Boxed`). What is less than `NEAR` (10 mm) in front of the eye is cut away: a triangle into the one or two its near part makes
314	(`Projector::in_front`, as weights of its corners, so a curve's lighting carries over), a line to its near part (`Camera::in_front`: edges in
315	wireframe, levels' marks, the section box's frame); a point behind the eye projects to no number. A face is lit on the side the eye is on
316	(`Camera::toward`), as the card's `front_facing` is, and how far a line may lie behind a surface and show is a pixel's worth where the
317	line is (`Camera::slack`). `Camera::along` takes, in perspective, the point on the axis nearest the line from the eye through the pointer,
318	so a dragged section box face stays under it. `render` of the 3D view goes through its lens, and `eye_elevation` puts the eye that high. A
319	sheet's 3D viewport stays parallel (its scale is paper's). The card draws perspective too: `View::perspective` gives the shader the
320	focal length, how far the eye is and a depth of `a + b / ahead`, 1 at `NEAR` and 0 past the far side of the mesh (a reversed depth, as
321	precise far off as near), with the same `NEAR` cut by the card's clipping; `Mesh::pick` cuts and projects as the processor does.
322	`picking_the_mesh_in_perspective_finds_what_the_cpu_picture_shows_from_afar_and_from_within` and
323	`the_card_draws_in_perspective_what_the_processor_does_from_afar_and_from_among_the_walls` compare them, from outside and with the eye
324	inside the house (`view3d::inside`).
325	
326	A 3D view may have a **camera of its own**, as Revit's Camera tool makes one: `View3D::camera`, a `ViewCamera` holding the model
327	point its `eye` stands at and the `target` it looks at (both `[x, y, z]` mm), with the view's `perspective` on. The `camera` command
328	makes a new named view from an eye and a target (the eye never on the target, checked in `Model::check`), gives one to an existing
329	view (the default `{3D}` among them, made by name as `perspective` makes it), or, with a `view` and none of `eye`, `target` or
330	`lens`, reads one back (`null` eye and target for a view with no camera yet — reading makes nothing). A view that already has a
331	camera keeps the point a change leaves out, so `lens` alone or one point alone changes just that; a view without one needs both.
332	`view3d::Camera::at` builds the render camera from the
333	eye, target and lens, its azimuth and elevation the direction from the eye to the target and `scale` the focal length over the
334	distance, so `Camera::eye` is exactly the eye given; `view3d::camera_of` does the same for a view and a scale, for a sheet's 3D
335	viewport. On the desktop the Camera tool (View tab) clicks an eye then a target in a plan, each at a height over it from the Options

461	dense pattern over an outline of thousands of corners and dots a twentieth of a millimetre apart. A pattern that gives up draws

473	renamed with their references (a type follows its patterns, a region its type and line style) and refused deleted while

482	A custom pattern is made of lines drawn, as pyRevit's Make Pattern makes one (`fills::make`, the `make_fill_pattern` command):
483	the detail lines picked, all of one view, cut to the rectangle between two corners (the tile), each a family that runs on into the
484	next tiles' copies of itself. A line repeats only at a slope `(i W, j H)` of whole tiles (`i`, `j` at most `MAX_STEPS`, 48), so one
485	drawn at another is turned to the simplest such slope within `TURN` (0.25°), else the nearest; its family's dashes are its length
486	and a space to the repeat `L = |(i W, j H)|`, its lines `W H / L` apart, each shifted along by the lattice's other vector
487	`(c W, d H)`, `i d - j c = 1` (Euclid's). A line on the tile's edge and its copy on the opposite one are one family; curves go as
488	their drawn points' chords. A model pattern is as drawn; a drafting one is the drawing on paper at the view's scale, which the
489	pattern keeps (`FillPattern::drawn`, saved with it): turned from one to the other (the dialog's Type, or `fill_pattern`'s `target`
490	without `lines`), it is rescaled (`retargeted`), and the dialog offers Redefine for it where a simple one has Edit Lines, which
491	picks the lines and corners again and keeps its name and type. A pattern holds at most `MAX_FAMILIES`
492	(256) families. In the desktop, New Pattern > Custom hides the dialog while the lines are picked as anything is (Enter, or the
493	right-click menu's Finish), then the corners (`Tool::PatternCorner`), and brings it back with the pattern previewed: OK, Pick
494	Again, Cancel. Esc, another tool or another view brings the dialog back. `pat.rs` reads and writes PAT files (`;%UNITS`,
495	`;%TYPE`, a negative offset stepping the other way; a pattern that can't be one left out with why) for the dialog and for the
496	`import_fill_patterns` and `export_fill_patterns` commands. A PAT file is hostile input: `read` stops after `MAX_PATTERNS`

550	level); a section or an elevation has no plan to snap to, only its own detail lines and regions. Of what the plan builds, the
551	nearest `MAX_OUTLINES` elements within reach have their outlines snapped to (one `walls::Index` for them all), and the nearest

575	
576	A `Link` element (`link.rs`; commands `link` and `reload`) is another project shown in this one as a reference. The file holds its name, its
577	path, where its origin stands (`at`) and a turn (`angle`); what it read is `Model::loaded`, by path, outside the file (`serde(skip)`), filled by
578	`link`, `reload` and `open` (`relink`, which doesn't follow the links of a linked file). The views draw `link::seen(model)`: the project with
579	each loaded link's built elements (`built`: not its views, sheets, annotation, detail lines, filled regions, detail groups, rooms, grids or links) moved and turned by `commands::transformed`
580	and brought in with `insert::insert_as(.., linked: true)` under ids from `LINKED` up (`ids.rs`), so `link::is_linked(id)` tells them; a level of the
581	link at the height of one of the project's (1 mm) is that level, another comes in named `link: level`. Everything that takes a `&Model` draws and snaps to
582	them without knowing: `Look::with` makes a linked id halftone, and picking never answers one (`Drawing::pick_all`, `in_box`, `Image::pick`,
583	`in_box`, `shows` and `Mesh::pick` leave them out). The commands that make an image (`render`, `save` to svg, png or pdf) draw `seen`; the desktop's
584	`view_model` does, cached by the project's `Arc`. The schedules, `Model::check`, IFC and every command that edits work on the project itself.
585	To do: shared coordinates, a link's graphics overrides and visibility per view, hosting on a linked wall, unloading.
586	
587	## Dimensions
588	
589	A dimension (`Dimension`, the `dimension` command) measures the model as it is, so it follows what it measures. Its `refs` are lines
590	(`Reference {id, face}`: a wall's centre line, faces and ends, a door's or window's centre and jambs, a grid, a straight detail line) or, with
591	`point: start|end`, the point at that end of one (`Model::reference_point`: a wall's centre line ends where its location line does, a face where
592	the outline turns off it, so at the mitred corner; a detail line of any shape at its ends; `reference_points` lists them, `endpoint_at` finds the
593	nearest, `{endpoint: [x, y]}` in a command). `reference_geometry` gives either as a line, a point as a line of no length, and `crossings` lays
594	them along the way the dimension measures (`measured_along`): a linear one's `orient` (horizontal or vertical), else square to its first line,
595	else from its first point to the next elsewhere. `Model::check` refuses a line not parallel to the first, or not square to a linear one's line,
596	and points all in one place. Mirror keeps the end of a line along the element and flips the one across it (`Reference::mirrored`); Flip swaps
597	both. A linear one given no `orient` runs vertical where `at` is east or west of everything it measures, else horizontal; the desktop's Auto
598	(`dims::Placing::kind`) also lays an aligned one where the cursor is among the points (`Orient::follow`), as Archicad does. Radial and diameter
599	dimensions measure round columns, curved walls (centre line or a face) and circles and arcs (`reference_arc`); arc length, a curved wall's or an
600	arc's length along it (`reference_sweep`), all of it or, with two point references after the arc, between them (`Model::arc_span`), its line an arc through `at` round the same centre. `dims::round_at` picks the face nearest a click.
601	
602	Each dimension has a dimension type (`dims.rs`, `Model::dimension_types`, a library entry `Kind::DimensionType`, the `dimension_type` command),
603	Revit's type parameters with lengths in mm on paper: Dimension String Type (continuous, baseline, ordinate), tick mark (diagonal, arrow, open
604	arrow, dot, none) and its size, line and tick pens, colour, dimension line extension, Witness Line Control (gap to element, or fixed to the
605	dimension line with its length), witness line gap and extension, baseline spacing, centre marks, and its text: font (as text types take one,
606	`DimensionType::lettering`), size, bold, italic, underline, width factor, offset, opaque or transparent background, Read Convention, units and
607	rounding (`DimensionType::length`), and the radius and diameter symbols and the equality text. A project starts with `Diagonal - 2.5mm Arial`,
608	which aligned, linear, angular and arc length dimensions start in, and `Arrow - 2.5mm Arial`, which radial and diameter ones do
609	(`dims::default_type`); a file of format 9 gives its dimensions their kind's (`Model::typed_dimensions`). A dimension's own text, Revit's
610	instance values, is a prefix, a suffix, text above and below, Replace With Text and Equality Display, and a segment may have its own over it
611	(`texts`, `SegmentText`, the `dimension_text` command; `Dimension::text` reads one through the other, `dimension_segment_at` finds a segment by a
612	point); `Model::dimension_labels` is what its
613	numbers read (and `elements` shows as `labels`): a baseline string's each from its first reference, an ordinate's each witness line's, the first 0.
614	An aligned or linear dimension may be kept equal (`equal`, Revit's EQ, which also turns its Equality Display on) and have segments
615	locked at a length (`locked`, `Lock`; the `dimension_constraint` command). `constraints::keep` runs in `Session::execute` after every undoable
616	command, before the check: each constrained dimension is solved on its own line (its `stations`, each with its reference), a locked segment tying
617	two stations rigidly and equality tying all its segments to one length (a locked one's, else its ends', which stay where they are, so an inner
618	reference dragged goes back); a run of tied stations stays where what the command moved puts it, else where its first is. What has to move is
619	moved by `commands::move_by`, as `move` moves it, and the dimensions are solved again (`PASSES`) until all hold; where they can't (locked
620	lengths that differ made equal, one element pulled two ways), the command is refused, saying which dimension, and nothing changes.
621	A length typed for a segment (`dimension_value`; in the window, a click on the selected dimension's number, as a temporary
622	dimension's takes one) moves what the segment ends at, its second station's reference, along the dimension by the difference
623	(`move_by`), and a locked segment is locked at it; the other locks then hold or the command is refused. Align with `lock` (Revit's
624	padlock: in the window, the open padlock Align offers on the line it moved) leaves a lock: a dimension of the aligned line's reference
625	and the reference's (`to`, else whatever has a line along it), its one segment locked at 0 and `alignment` set, which
626	`constraints::keep` holds as it holds the others, so the two lines stay on one line whatever either is moved by; one that can't hold
627	with the other locks is refused, and the project is as it was. A lock is drawn by a front end, never on paper (`render/dimensions.rs`
628	draws nothing of it): the window shows each locked segment's shut padlock whether its dimension is selected or not, and each alignment
629	lock's padlock beside where its lines meet, which a click unlocks (deletes). Format 15 holds them; 14 would read one as a dimension of
630	nothing.
631	`render/dimensions.rs` draws them all as the type says (`Ink`: its lines, ticks and witness lines, and its numbers laid out by `crate::text`
632	over the paper where the background is opaque).
633	
634	A 3D view has dimensions of its own (`Element::Dimension3D`, the `dimension_3d` command; `dims3d.rs`), as Revit's aligned dimension in a 3D
635	view: two references (`Ref3`), each a point of the model or a point on an edge (its two ends with it), and a point its line passes through,
636	kept by the view (`view`, a GUID: deleting the view takes them with it) and of a dimension type as a plan's are. Between two points it measures
637	straight from one to the other; to an edge, square to the edge's line, so between two parallel edges it is how far apart they are
638	(`dims3d::ends`). They hold places in space, not references to elements: moving an element leaves them, and `move`, `rotate` and `mirror`
639	take them in plan when they are moved themselves. They draw as marks (`dims3d::marks`, `Mark`: a polyline in the picture's pixels, its width
640	and colour), through any camera and at any paper size (`SCREEN` pixels a paper millimetre on screen, `sheet::DENSITY` on a sheet): a
641	witness line from each end of what it measures to its line, its line, a tick at each end and its number lettered along it in our strokes
642	(`font.rs`), reading from the left, on the side away from what it measures; nothing hides them. `dims3d::paint` paints marks into the
643	processor's picture, which the `render` command does for a 3D view; a sheet draws them as its own lines over the view's picture, so they print
644	in its PDF; the window draws them over the picture on either painter (the card's too) with the theme's ink, the selection's colour when
645	picked. Visibility/Graphics hides them with Dimensions (`category_of`). In the window the Aligned Dimension tool (DI) in the 3D view picks a
646	corner seen within the snap's reach (`Scene::corner_near`), else an edge within a pick's (`Scene::edge_near`, the point of it nearest the
647	cursor), else the point of the face there; after two, a click places the line where it meets the plane through the two that faces the
648	camera most (`dims3d::line_through`), and the status line says how long it is. In Modify a click on a dimension's lines picks it before what
649	the picture shows under them (`dims3d::pick`).

fn usage_exit(prefix: Option<String>) -> ! {
    if let Some(p) = prefix {

    }
    eprint!("{}", catalog::USAGE);
    exit(1);

    if args.is_empty() {

            println!("bimcraft-cli {}", VERSION);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run each command line of a file (or stdin) separately on the original (and optionally mine).
usage: each.py [-m] [-b] [-f in.bimcraft] [-s 'setup cmd']... < cmds.txt
  -m: run mine instead; -b: run both and mark differences; -f: open this project first.
Each line: a command `id {json}` (or several separated by ' ;; ')."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, re
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae7e467313951842e/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
G = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
a = sys.argv[1:]
exes = [ORIG]
infile = None
setup = []
both = False
while a:
    if a[0] == '-m': exes = [MINE]; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-b': exes = [ORIG, MINE]; both = True; a = a[1:]
    elif a[0] == '-f': infile = a[1]; a = a[2:]
    elif a[0] == '-s': setup.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
    else: break
lines = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in sys.stdin if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
def norm(s):
    m = {}
    def rep(mo):
        g = mo.group(0)
        if g not in m: m[g] = 'GUID-%d' % (len(m) + 1)
        return m[g]
    return G.sub(rep, s)
same = 0
for l in lines:
    outs = []
    for exe in exes:
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='e', dir='/tmp/views-agent')
        args = [exe, 'run']
        if infile:
            shutil.copy(infile, d)
            args.append(os.path.basename(infile))
        for s in setup:
            args += ['--cmd', s]
        for c in l.split(' ;; '):
            args += ['--cmd', c]
        p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, timeout=120)
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        o = p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip().split('\n')
        o = [x for x in o if x][-1:] if (infile or setup) else o
        outs.append(norm(('OUT ' + '\n    '.join(o) if any(o) else '') + (' ERR ' + p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip() if p.stderr else '') + ' [%d]' % p.returncode))
    if both:
        if outs[0] == outs[1]:
            same += 1
            print('SAME', l[:150])
        else:
            print('DIFF', l)
            print('  orig:', outs[0])
            print('  mine:', outs[1])
    else:
        print('>>', l)
        print('  ', outs[0])
if both:
    print('%d/%d same' % (same, len(lines)))
